procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and Order dated 26.10.2021 of the High Court of Judicature at Madras in CRLA No.176 of 2017
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The Appellant preferred an appeal (Criminal Appeal No. 176 of 2017) before the High Court of Judicature at Madras, challenging the Sessions Court's judgment dated 03.02.2017, which convicted the Appellant for offences under the POCSO Act. The High Court dismissed the appeal and confirmed the Sessions Court's judgment.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The Appellant approached the Supreme Court, aggrieved by the High Court's judgment dated 26.10.2021. The Supreme Court initially issued notice only on the quantum of sentence awarded to the Appellant, limiting the scope of its review.

decision.conviction_status: The conviction of the Appellant u/s. 3(a) r/w Sec. 4 of the POCSO Act, 2012 is confirmed.
decision.sentence_status: The sentence imposed by the Sessions Court and confirmed by the High Court is modified and reduced to the period already undergone by the Appellant.
directions: The Appellant be set at liberty forthwith in case he is not required in any other case.

issue.issue_text: Whether the conviction of the Appellant for offences under Section 3(a) read with Section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, should be upheld.

facts: The Appellant was convicted by the Sessions Court for offences under Section 3(a) read with Section 4 of the POCSO Act, 2012.
This conviction was confirmed by the High Court.
The Supreme Court issued a notice limiting the scope of the appeal to only the 'quantum of sentence awarded to the Appellant'.
application: The Supreme Court noted that its review was restricted to the limited question of the sentence and not the conviction itself.
Therefore, the court did not re-examine the merits of the conviction as decided by the lower courts.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court explicitly confirmed and upheld the conviction of the Appellant under Section 3(a) read with Section 4 of the POCSO Act, 2012. While the court proceeded to modify the sentence, the conviction itself was left undisturbed.

issue.issue_text: Whether the sentence of ten years of rigorous imprisonment imposed on the Appellant is excessive and requires modification.

facts: The appellant was convicted under sections 3(a) and 4 of the POCSO Act and sentenced to ten years of rigorous imprisonment.
The Supreme Court's review was limited only to the question of whether the sentence was excessive, not the conviction itself.

The appellant's lawyer argued for leniency on two main grounds: first, that the appellant had already served more than the seven-year minimum sentence that was in effect at the time of his conviction.
Second, the lawyer submitted that the appellant was financially supporting the victim and her child, and his continued imprisonment would negatively impact them.
application: The Court considered the "totality of the circumstances" of the case.

It took into account the arguments presented by the appellant's counsel, specifically that he had already served more than the minimum sentence and was providing financial support to the victim and her child.
reasoning.conclusion: Based on the totality of the circumstances, the Court decided that the "ends of justice" would be met by reducing the sentence. While it upheld the conviction, it modified the sentence to the period the appellant had already served in prison and ordered his release.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the sentence of ten years of rigorous imprisonment imposed on the Appellant is excessive and requires modification.
appellant_arguments: The appellant has already served more than the seven-year minimum sentence that was prescribed under the POCSO Act at the time of the conviction.
The appellant is providing for the day-to-day expenses of the victim and her child.

statutes.act_name: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012

ratio_decidendi.ratio: An appellate court may, based on the totality of the circumstances of a case, modify and reduce a sentence of imprisonment to the period already undergone by the appellant in order to meet the ends of justice, even while confirming the conviction.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: Having heard the Learned Counsel for the parties and considering the totality of the circumstances of the case, we are of the view that the ends of justice would be met if the period of imprisonment awarded against the Appellant is reduced to the period already undergone by him.
why_appellant_lost: The Supreme Court's review was procedurally limited to the quantum of sentence, as it had issued notice only on that specific question. Therefore, the merits of the conviction were not considered or re-examined.
why_respondent_won: The conviction was upheld because the Court's review was confined solely to the issue of sentencing, meaning the challenge to the conviction itself was not before the Court for consideration.
policy_considerations: The court considered the practical and financial impact of further imprisonment, noting the appellant's submission that he is providing for the day-to-day expenses of the victim and her child, and that continued incarceration would negatively impact both families.

The court weighed the fact that the appellant had already served more than the seven-year minimum sentence that was prescribed under the POCSO Act at the time of the conviction when deciding to show leniency.
